sentences.text:
Kapil Katiyar And 3 Ohters vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21
February, 2023
Author: Dinesh Kumar Singh

Bench: Dinesh Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 87
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 3584 of 2021
Applicant :- Kapil Katiyar And 3 Ohters

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Anand Kumar Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
Heard Sri Anand Kumar Singh learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State respondents.

The present bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking anticipatory bail in anticipation of his arrest in Case Crime No. 39 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Kalyanpur, District Kanpur Nagar.
Sri Sanjay Singh, learned A.G.A. submits that in the aforesaid case crime number, charge-sheet has already been filed.

It is further submitted that all alleged offences are punishable with imprisonment for less than seven years, therefore the police authorities are bound to follow the procedure laid down under Section Kapil Katiyar And 3 Ohters vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182846478/
1 41-A Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Section Kapil Katiyar And 3 Ohters vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: The applicants have been wrongly implicated and could not be arrested.

Reliance has been placed on the judgement of Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273 and Social Action Forum for Manav Adhikar Vs. Union of India, Ministry of Law and Justice and others in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 73 of 2015 with Criminal Appeal No. 1265 of 2017, Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 156 of 2017, Satendra Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another,
(2022) 10 SCC 51 and co-ordinate Division Bench of this Court in Vimal Kumar & 3 others Vs. State of U.P. & 3 others in 2021 (2) ACR 1147.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Reliance has been placed on the judgement of Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273 and Social Action Forum for Manav Adhikar Vs. Union of India, Ministry of Law and Justice and others in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 73 of 2015 with Criminal Appeal No. 1265 of 2017, Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 156 of 2017, Satendra Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another,

opennyai_summary.decision:
In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.
The accused-applicant is directed to appear before the trial Court concerned within ten days from today and if he does so, he shall be released on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, on the following conditions, which are imposed in the interest of justice, and other conditions, which may be desirable by the learned trial Court:-
(i) That the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii) That the applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer;
(iii) That the applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court; and (iv) Such other conditions as may be imposed under sub-section (3) of Section 437, as if the bail were granted under that section.
It is made clear that observations made herein-above are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial or deciding the regular bail application.
Order Date :- 21.2.2023
